https://www.politico.eu/article/us-court.text: BRUSSELS — How do you solve a monopoly like Google’s? It’s a question that has beset Brussels for the past year, ever since the European Commission fined the search giant €2.95 billion for monopolizing the vast market for digital advertising. A few months earlier, in April 2025, a U.S. judge had also found Google guilty in a lawsuit brought by the Department of Justice (DoJ), as parallel investigations on both sides of the Atlantic finally ran their course. On Wednesday, however, the same U.S. judge made the European Commission’s life a lot more difficult. Advertisement Advertisement In a ruling from Washington’s own attempt to break up Google, Judge Leonie Brinkema, of the Federal District of Eastern Virginia, rejected the DoJ’s request for a forced divestiture of parts of its business. That decision leaves the EU alone, at a time of transatlantic discord, in advocating that the online advertising giant break itself up. “It’s obvious that the European Commission has been holding out for a decision in the parallel U.S. case, even if it has the authority to act independently and should have done so long ago,” Max von Thun, Europe director at the Open Markets Institute non-profit, told POLITICO. One year after the Commission issued its fine, both the complainants who brought the case, and the civil society groups who see this as a test of the EU’s nerve in confronting Big Tech, fear the EU executive may find itself with limited options to loosen Google’s stranglehold on the online advertising ecosystem. “As long as Google maintains the incentive and the means, they have an endless number of paths to achieve comparable anti-competitive goals,” said Arielle Garcia, CEO of Check My Ads, a U.S.-based watchdog, adding that while a Europe-only remedy might be technically possible, its effect would be minimal. In her order, Brinkema said she didn’t see a structural divestment of part of Google’s business as necessary to remedy the finding of liability against the company. Advertisement Advertisement Last September, in a parallel decision, the Commission said a divestment appeared to be the only way to resolve Google’s inherent conflict of interest. Making the best of it Among those who brought the case, the mood is resigned. Several people involved in the complaint said privately that they no longer see a viable way to carve out and sell part of a U.S. company’s business within Europe alone, and are now pushing for the strongest measures the Commission can realistically deliver. “There was such an expectation that breakup was going to change the world. It was never going to change the world. The key critical issue is what you do about non-discrimination,” said Tim Cowen, a partner at Preiskel & Co., who represents a complainant in the case. The obstacle to a breakup is as much structural as it is political. Google’s buying tools, selling tools and the exchange between them run as one global system. A sale ordered by Brussels would apply on one side of the Atlantic, in a market where the largest advertisers and publishers don’t stop at the EU’s borders. The Commission recognizes some of those difficulties. Advertisement Advertisement Structural remedies in cases where parties have already completed investment activities “are of course very difficult and can be politically contested,” said DG Competition’s Director General Anthony Whelan at a conference in Florence on Friday. “Irrespective of the context of transatlantic relations, of course, this is a difficult case,” Whelan added. The EU executive is still assessing Google’s compliance plan, having granted the firm an extension within the deadline for assessing its proposal back in March. The extension was meant to give the Commission time to analyze Google’s plan “in depth” and take a view on whether it is compliant, said Ricardo Cardoso, a spokesperson for the EU executive. Google submitted the plan in November 2025, proposing changes to how its tools work rather than a sale. Ribera called the offer serious as the Commission put it to industry for comment. The Trump administration has repeatedly threatened tariffs over the EU’s actions against U.S. tech companies, and last year opened a trade investigation a day after Brussels fined Google under its digital rulebook. Advertisement Advertisement “One year on, those conflicts of interest remain,” said Andreas Schwab, a German lawmaker with the center-right European People’s Party. “Instead of taking action, [the Commission] continues to give Google more time to extend its market power.” Schuman showdown Campaigners marked the one-year anniversary of the Brussels Google fine on Friday at the Schuman roundabout, where they pelted a Google logo with fake money. A coalition of non-profits including People vs Big Tech, LobbyControl, Rebalance Now, WeMove Europe and the Balanced Economy Project puts Google’s EU revenues at €288 million a day since the ruling dropped, based on filings in 19 member countries compiled by the Media and Journalism Research Center. The figure covers Google’s whole EU business, not just advertising. Nienke Palstra, of the People vs Big Tech civil society network, said the case has become a test of Europe’s courage, and that every day the Commission delays, Google consolidates its position. “Google has shown it will not act of its own accord to make the changes needed and the Commission must step up,” Max Bank, EU competition lead at Rebalance Now, told POLITICO. Von Thun from the Open Markets Institute went further. “Instead of following this misguided decision by Judge Brinkema, the Commission must now show global leadership by imposing the structural remedies that are needed,” he said. Advertisement Advertisement “As always, we stand ready to hear the views of civil society groups and consumers,” a Commission spokesperson told POLITICO on Friday, adding that they continue their investigation in the Google Adtech case “as a matter of priority.” Google is appealing the Commission's decision at the EU’s General Court, and said Wednesday it was “very pleased” with the U.S. ruling. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the extension. With reporting from Francesca Micheletti in Florence.

https://telex.hu/transtelex/2026/10/20/k.text: Menü Kereső Majdnem fél év kormányválság után megszavazta az új kabinetet a román parlament Transtelex A szociáldemokraták és Luca Niculescu független kormányfő ünnepelnek a parlamentben, miután majdnem fél év kormányválság után megszavazták az új kormányt 2026. október 20-án – Fotó: George Călin / Inquam Photos Zsizsmann Erika (Transtelex) Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom 280 támogató és 58 ellenszavazattal megszavazta a független Luca Niculescu kormányát a román parlament. A 12 szociáldemokrata és 6 független technokrata miniszterből álló kisebbségi kabinetet a Szociáldemokrata Párt (PSD) mellett a Nemzeti Liberális Párt (PNL), az RMDSZ, a nemzeti kisebbségek frakciója, valamint az Egységben Romániáért (UPR) frakció támogatta. Niculescu és miniszterei a tervek szerint már kedden este megtartják az első kormányülést, miután leteszik az esküt Nicușor Dan államfő előtt. Az új kormányfő az utóbbi négy évben Románia OECD-csatlakozását koordinálta külügyi államtitkárként, 2016–2022 között pedig Románia párizsi nagyköveteként dolgozott, eredetileg pedig újságíró, az RFI Románia főszerkesztőjeként dolgozott, és több jelentős francia sajtóorgánum romániai tudósítója is volt. A szociáldemokraták köré tömörülő kormány névsora jelentős felháborodást váltott ki , különösen azért, mert a miniszterelnök-helyettes és belügyminiszter az a Marian Neacșu lesz, akit korábban jogerősen elítéltek bűncselekménynek minősülő összeférhetetlenség miatt, az igazságügyi miniszter pedig a plágiummal vádolt Radu Marinescu lesz. Az új kormány beiktatásához szükséges többség végül úgy állt össze, hogy a PNL és az RMDSZ is vállalta, hogy külön megállapodásokban rögzített feltételek mellett megszavazzák a kabinetet, de ellenzékbe vonulnak. A Niculescu-kormány támogatása komoly vitákat váltott ki a PNL-en belül , de a párt elnöke, Ilie Bolojan végül keresztülvitte a döntést, azzal érvelve, hogy öt hónapnyi bizonytalanság után már az alapvető közszolgáltatások működése is veszélybe kerülhet, ha nem lesz teljes jogkörrel bíró kormánya Romániának. A beiktatást megelőző parlamenti vitán a liberálisok hangsúlyozták, hogy csupán kényszerből, az ország működőképességének megőrzése és a politikai krízis lezárása érdekében szavaztak igennel, az RMDSZ elnöke is azt emelte ki, hogy felelősségből írt alá hat hónapra szóló politikai megállapodást Luca Niculescuval , amellyel a kormány működését és a magyar közösség érdekeinek védelmét szeretné biztosítani. A leköszönő Bolojan-kormányban is részt vevő, progresszív Mentsétek Meg Romániát Szövetség (USR) élesen kirohant a szociáldemokraták ellen, mielőtt képviselői nemmel szavaztak volna. A nacionalista Románok Egyesüléséért Szövetség (AUR) bojkottálta a szavazást, és kivonult a teremből. Ez volt a negyedik próbálkozás a kormányalakításra, miután a liberális Ilie Bolojan kormányát a koalícióból kilépő PSD a szélsőjobboldali AUR-ral közös bizalmatlansági indítvánnyal május 5-én megbuktatta . Az első kormányfőjelölt, Eugen Tomac támogatás híján visszalépett, ezután Nicușor Dan államfő liberális Adrian Veșteát kérte fel kormányalakításra, de anélkül, hogy egyeztetett volna a párt elnökével, Ilie Bolojannal, amivel jelentős belső harcot indított el a PNL-ben. Veștea kabinetjét június 22-én leszavazta a parlament . A nyár meddő tárgyalásokkal telt el, szeptember közepén pedig Siegfried Mureșan liberális EP-képviselőt, a PNL, az USR és az RMDSZ közös miniszterelnök-jelöltjét kérte fel kormányalakításra az államfő , de ahogy az várható volt, ő sem kapott elég szavazatot a parlamentben. Glocal Equality and Hospitality (Invalidated Ideas?) August 7–December 7, 2026 Add to Calendar Lecture by Hito Steyerl, “Ruins at Scale”: November 11, 6:30pm Cultural Creative Center Hviezda, Kniežaťa Pribinu 3, Trenčín, Slovakia Add to Calendar Lecture by Cooking Sections, “Wallowland”: November 19, 6pm Cultural Creative Center Hviezda, Kniežaťa Pribinu 3, Trenčín, Slovakia Add to Calendar RSVP County House (Župný dom) Mierové Square 46 Trenčín Slovakia www.trencin2026.eu Instagram / Facebook / YouTube Trenčín 2026–European Capital of Culture presents Glocal Equality and Hospitality (Invalidated Ideas?) , a group exhibition at the newly renovated County House (Župný dom) in Trenčín, Slovakia. Bringing together internationally recognised artists and collectives, the exhibition reflects on urgent and interconnected 'glocal' challenges—from social and economic inequality to migration, ecological crisis, and rising geopolitical tensions. Through a range of site-specific works and commissioned projects, it proposes art as a space for critical reflection, solidarity, and alternative ways of understanding the present. The exhibition evolved from the curators' project, Universal Hospitality (Vienna and Prague, 2015–16), which explored themes of nationalism and populism in the context of the refugee crisis. Over time, many other issues have come to light, making it increasingly difficult to identify a single pressing concern: the challenges facing contemporary societies are interconnected. " The title’s use of the word ‘glocal’ reflects the exhibition’s attempt to connect global processes with their local forms and consequences. Equality is understood both in relation to individual lives and to relationships between countries, communities, and power structures. Hospitality, meanwhile, is expanded beyond human relations to encompass the way we treat other living beings and the environment. In this sense, the exhibition asks whether the ideals of the Enlightenment still provide a meaningful framework for understanding the world today, or whether we have entered a different and more uncertain era ," said curators Edit András and Ilona Németh . The exhibition brings together works by Marco Scotini (Italy), Kateryna Aliinyk (Ukraine), Anca Benera & Arnold Estefán (Romania/Austria), András Cséfalvay (Slovakia), Hito Steyerl (Germany), Ferenc Gróf & Zsófia Gyenes (France/Hungary), Sanja Iveković (Croatia), Szabolcs KissPál (Hungary), Zdena Kolečková (Czech Republic), Oliver Ressler (Austria), Emilia Rigová (Slovakia), Lucia Tkáčová (Slovakia), Martin Zetová (Czech Republic), Artur Żmijewski (Poland), Jaro Varga (Slovakia), as well as the Border Emergency Collective (Poland). Through installations, paintings, sculptures, videos, and textiles, the works bring global issues into focus through both macro and micro perspectives. International artists who have been exhibited at the Venice Biennale are part of the exhibition, including Marco Scotini and his work Disobedience Archive, which was shown at the Venice Biennale in 2024, as well as Anca Benera and Arnold Estefán, who are represented in a solo exhibition in the Romanian Pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale. One of Hito Steyerl’s newest works, a mesmerizing video installation, is also on display. At the heart of the exhibition lies Disobedience Archive , which provides a panoramic view of our turbulent times through the lens of social movements and collective action. Renowned international artists explore themes such as economic and social inequalities, gender imbalances, the oppression of minorities, and the escalating impact of the ecological crisis, inviting visitors to consider the complex challenges shaping the contemporary world. The global landscape is marked by heightened geopolitical tensions, wars, and expansionism, all of which are explored in the exhibition through the ways in which they shape local realities. Other works also consider the impact of our technology-, social media-, and AI-driven environment, exploring how these factors shape our world and our relationship with technology. The exhibition also explores the origins of the present-day challenges through a journey back to the socialist era. Meanwhile, some works offer a glimpse into the future or propose alternative ideas for responding to complex issues facing societies from both global and local perspectives. These works invite reflection on solidarity, radical care and greater awareness of minorities and marginalized groups. The exhibition is accompanied by a programme of events and performances. On November 11 at Cultural and Creative Centre Hviezda, German artist, filmmaker and theorist Hito Steyerl will discuss her artistic practice and present Mechanical Kurds , her work featured in the exhibition. Global Equality and Hospitality is part of the programme European Capital of Culture Trenčín 2026. Trenčín 2026 is financially supported by the City of Trenčín, the Trenčín Self-Governing Region, and the Ministry of Culture of the Slovak Republic. The European Union is a partner of Trenčín 2026. https://www.adweek.com/tvnewser/ticker-n.text: Top of the Ticker: NBC News’ long-running investigative series Dateline is getting a clone in Canada, with Dateline Canada debuting on Citytv and Citytv+ on Thursday, November 26. This marks the true-crime franchise's first international expansion under a licensing deal with Rogers Studios. Diana Swain, a former CBC News senior investigative correspondent and current host of The Investigators on CBC News Network, will host the spinoff. The premiere episode, which is two hours long, looks into the disappearance of Elizabeth Bain, a University of Toronto student who went missing in 1990. Keith Morrison, who hosts the U.S. version, began his journalism career in Canada, where he is from, and previously worked with CTV and CBC News. Data center backlash: MS NOW anchor Ali Velshi will, on Sunday night at 10 p.m. ET, host a new special on the growing nationwide backlash to data centers and A.I. Sparking Outrage: Data Center and A.I. Backlash will feature reporting from MS NOW senior reporter Josh Einiger, with the topic becoming one of the key issues of next month’s midterm elections. Meanwhile, the network made an on-air apology on Wednesday after falsely reporting that FBI director Kash Patel had traveled to Russia to meet with officials. Justice correspondent Ken Dilanian, who filed the initial report citing two anonymous FBI sources, issued the apology later that day, saying, “We regret this error, and we are transparent about when we make errors.” New partnership: CNN this week announced it will be participating in Google’s news A.I. pilot program. The network said this multi-year partnership will provide enhanced content rights, enabling experimental features in Google products to help explore how generative A.I. can create additional engagement for its journalism. In other news, CNN announced that its direct-to-consumer (DTC) subscription product, CNN All Access, will be expanding to Canada and the United Kingdom beginning October 20. CNN All Access, which has been live in the U.S. for nearly a year, will cost $7.99 CAD per month or $79.99 CAD annually. In the U.K., it'll cost £4.99 per month or £49.99 annually. Online availability: U.S. viewers with a bigger appetite for international news can now grab a bigger plate as the BBC announced its flagship news channel, BBC News, will be available on YouTube. BBC says this is part of a wider strategy to reach digitally native, younger audiences. The U.S. joins Australia, Kenya, Nigeria, and Poland in gaining access to BBC News via YouTube. Awards: On Wednesday night, MS NOW’s senior contributing editor, Michele Norris, received the Freedom of the Press Career Achievement Award at the 2026 RCFP Freedom of the Press Awards. In accepting her award, Norris also honored journalists, including those at MS NOW, who have stood up to efforts to silence the press, saying the battle over freedom of the press is one journalists have been there before and “is not new ground.”
